title: BenchX work order
description: The runner's single input: what to run, against which target, how, and for whom. A runner executes one work order per invocation. See docs/design/work-order.md. The order carries only what its author decides; everything the runner can observe is captured by the runner, and comparison identity and series are never part of it.
$comment: Rules the schema cannot express and the runner enforces: target paths are absolute; the suite exists in the target; filter and suite use the named harness's syntax; every listed quantity is one the adapter can map; a setting the runner cannot apply is rejected, not ignored; every setting the runner does apply is recorded in the result it produces. Shared types are references into urn:benchx:schema:measurement-result:0.1.0, which validators must load alongside this schema, so every value the runner copies into results is valid there by construction.

workorder_version.description: Work order contract version this object conforms to. Named differently from a result's schema_version so a loader can tell the two kinds apart.

project.description: Namespace for project-defined names and policy, copied to each result's project. Omit for an ad hoc run; its results are thin (result schema section 4.1).

source.description: Designated subject source whose revisions form the history axis, copied to each result's source.

harness.description: Harness that runs the suite. Selects the adapter and fixes how suite, filter, and protocol keys are read. Recorded in each result's comparison_context.

name.description: Harness name, such as google-benchmark or pyperf. An open value: the runner rejects a name it has no adapter for.

version.description: Harness version the order requires, if any. The runner records the version it ran.

target.description: Where the code to measure lives. One of two kinds; a revision to build and a prebuilt artifact are future kinds.

build_dir.description: Absolute path of the build directory holding the suite. The runner captures the build configuration from it into coordinates.subject.configuration.

python.description: Absolute path of the Python interpreter that runs the suite, with the subject and the harness installed. The runner captures the interpreter version, implementation, and build flags.

suite.description: Suite to execute; for Google Benchmark, the benchmark binary's name inside target.build_dir.

filter.description: Case filter in the harness's syntax, such as a Google Benchmark --benchmark_filter regular expression. Omit to run the whole suite.

quantities.description: Quantity names to emit. Each becomes coordinates.quantity.name of one result per case; results for one case from one invocation share an attempt_key. Units come from the adapter mapping.

protocol.description: Intended acquisition settings, in the result schema's Appendix B spellings, copied verbatim into each result's comparison_context.protocol; realized counterparts go to procedure. The runner fills in every setting it applies and rejects a key it cannot apply, so no applied setting goes unrecorded. This is the one open object in a work order: harness-specific keys pass through unchanged.

repetitions.description: Independent repetitions of one case, outermost level first. One level for a harness that repeats inside a single process (Google Benchmark); two for one that also spawns processes (pyperf).

unit.description: What one repetition at this level is: repetition, process, value. An open value.

calibration.description: How the iteration count inside one repetition is chosen: adaptive to a minimum sample duration, or fixed by the author.

warmup.description: Discarded measurements before the recorded ones.

provenance.description: Who ordered the run and why. Nothing here enters comparison identity.

run_key.description: Grouping key assigned by the run author, who is this order's author. Copied to provenance.run_key of every result.

labels.description: Caller-supplied labels for selecting sides of a comparison, such as {"side": "baseline"}. Copied to provenance.labels.

requested_by.description: Person or system that requested the run. Result provenance has no field for it, so the runner records it as provenance.info.requested_by.

reason.description: Free-text reason for the run, recorded as provenance.info.reason.

sourceDir.description: Absolute path of the checkout the target was built or installed from. The runner captures revision.key, provenance.subject_dirty, and provenance.subject_tree from it; if it cannot locate the checkout, subject_dirty is unknown and subject_tree is absent.
